proposal.name: Mark a draft ready before merging it, and say a refused merge once

plan.name: Mark a draft ready before merging it, and say a refused merge once
plan.summary: On copythis-ad#36 the factory tried to merge its draft pull request every poll for seven minutes, because GitHub refuses to merge a draft and the factory never marks one ready (#145). Now, once the protocol and the recovery core allow a merge and the merge is recorded, the factory marks a draft ready for review and merges it in the same poll, and merges only if marking it ready succeeded: the `GitHub` interface gains `MarkReady(ctx context.Context, n int) error`, which `github.Client` does by reading the pull request's `node_id` from `GET repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}` and running GraphQL's `markPullRequestReadyForReview` mutation on it through `gh api graphql`, as `MergeCommits` asks GraphQL, since the REST API can't take a pull request out of draft; `leasedGitHub` checks the lease before it, and the tests' `fakeGitHub` gains it too, with its `Merge` refusing a draft as GitHub does. When GitHub refuses to mark the draft ready or to merge, the factory says so on the issue once, in a failed post with a new failure, `FailMerge` (`merge`), that names the pull request, quotes GitHub's answer, labels the issue `invariant:human-review-needed` and says to comment `/invariant retry` once the cause is fixed, and the step ends without an error (only a lost lease or an ended context is returned as one instead); the protocol sees that post as a pull request the factory can't merge, out of scope with its failure counted as `unmergeable`, as it sees a change to the trusted base (D-0105), the recovery core sees one GitHub can't merge, and nothing is tried again until a writer's retry has the factory watch the pull request again. Because the record of the refused attempt stays, a merge the factory finds counts as its own only while its latest post is the pull request's (`pr`), so when a person merges after a refusal, the factory records that it was merged, not that it merged it. A build that passed (for a plan, passed and approved) and finds a draft already open from its branch, opened without this build's result, marks it ready before it says the pull request is open, logging a refusal and going on, since the merge marks it ready again; everything else stays as it is, including the draft a failed build opens.

tests.name: TestADraftWhoseGatePassedAfterARetryIsMarkedReadyAndMerged
tests.says: A build fails the gate and leaves a draft, CI's gate passes on it, and a writer says retry, against a GitHub that refuses to merge a draft. The factory asks nothing of the draft until the protocol allows the merge, and then, in the one poll after it answers the retry, it marks the draft ready for review and merges it.

tests.name: TestAMergeGitHubRefusesIsSaidOnce
tests.says: When GitHub refuses the merge, or refuses to mark a draft ready and nothing is merged, the poll ends without an error and one failed post, labeled for a person, with failure `merge`, names the pull request, quotes GitHub's answer and says to comment `/invariant retry`. Three more polls post nothing and ask GitHub nothing, and once a writer says retry, the factory tries again and merges.

tests.name: TestAPersonMergesWhatGitHubRefusedTheFactory
tests.says: After the factory says GitHub refused its merge, a person merges the pull request on GitHub, and the next poll records that it was merged, not as the factory's own merge, without an error or another attempt of the factory's.

tests.name: TestABuildThatPassedMarksADraftOpenFromItsBranchReady
tests.says: A build stops, a draft is opened from its branch, and a writer's retry builds again and passes. The factory takes that draft as its pull request, opens no other, marks it ready for review before it says the pull request is open, and merges it once CI's gate passes.

tests.name: TestMarkReadyRunsGraphQLsMutationOnThePullRequest
tests.says: `Client.MarkReady` runs GraphQL's `markPullRequestReadyForReview` through gh on the pull request's node ID, and returns no error when GitHub accepts it, and an error that quotes GitHub when it refuses.

usage.summary:
I've written the plan for #145, and the check passed on the first run: all 5 acceptance tests fail on the code as it is, and since it touches the factory, a person merges it. Before merging, the factory now marks a draft ready for review and merges it in the same poll. If GitHub refuses, it says so once on the issue (new failure `merge`) and waits for a writer's `/invariant retry`; the plan also covers the issue's third point, a passing build that finds a draft already open from its branch.

Choices I made that you should know about before ratifying:

- **Protocol mapping.** The ratified protocol has no step for "GitHub refused a merge". The plan reports a refusal to it as a pull request the factory can't merge (out of scope, failure `unmergeable`), the same way it already treats a change to the trusted base (D-0105). The protocol itself isn't changed.
- **A fix the issue didn't ask for.** After a refused merge, the factory's record of its attempt stays behind. Without a change, a person merging the pull request by hand would be claimed as the factory's merge, which the protocol refuses, so the issue would be stuck on every poll. The plan counts a merge as the factory's only while its latest post is the pull request's, and one test covers this.
- **Marking ready through GraphQL.** The GitHub client uses GraphQL's `markPullRequestReadyForReview`, because GitHub's REST API accepts `draft: false` without changing anything. One test makes sure it doesn't take the REST route.
- **The third point is best effort.** If GitHub won't mark the leftover draft ready at build time, the factory logs it and moves on, and tries again before merging, so that step never retries on every poll. It doesn't turn a non-draft into a draft when a build fails, since that wasn't what the issue was about.

The plan is in `plan.json`, and the tests are in `tests/internal/factory/draftmerge_accept_test.go` and `tests/internal/github/ready_accept_test.go`.
